title: Self-financed multi-decade power deals reach a second frontier lab by H2 2027
body: OpenAI's Project Camellia, unveiled July 22, is less notable for its size - a four-building Effingham County, Georgia campus drawing 3.2 gigawatts, backed by at least $20 billion and reported above $30 billion at full build - than for how the power is bought. OpenAI signed a 25-year supply agreement with Georgia Power, committed to pay the full cost of the electrical infrastructure so existing ratepayers are shielded, and offered up to a gigawatt of flexible demand response to steady the regional grid. That is a frontier lab taking direct control of power procurement and financing the grid itself, not renting space and letting a utility carry the interconnection. The prediction is that this structure - a multi-decade direct utility supply agreement, plus lab-funded electrical infrastructure, plus an explicit ratepayer-protection or demand-response commitment, at gigawatt scale - stops being an OpenAI signature and becomes the template a second named frontier-scale operator publicly adopts by H2 2027. The forcing function is stated in the news itself: grid interconnection, not GPU supply, is now the binding constraint on frontier-scale compute, and the queue for large-load hookups runs years. A lab that will not wait, and that faces regulators increasingly unwilling to let data centers shift transmission costs onto households, has to internalize the power problem - sign directly for decades of supply, pay for its own substations and lines, and offer the grid flexibility in return - exactly the concessions Camellia front-ran. Once one lab shows utilities and public-service commissions that shape of deal, it becomes the price of entry the next gigawatt campus is negotiated against. The prediction is falsified if, through H2 2027, no other frontier operator - among Anthropic, xAI, Meta, Google or a named Stargate-class competitor - discloses a gigawatt-scale campus under a multi-year direct utility supply agreement in which the lab funds its own grid interconnection and accepts a ratepayer-shield or large-scale demand-response term, and such self-financed power structures remain particular to OpenAI while peers keep buying conventional grid-supplied capacity or short renewable offtake.

reasoning.because: OpenAI's Camellia signs a 25-year Georgia Power deal and self-funds the grid to shield ratepayers
reasoning.given: Grid interconnection, not GPUs, is the binding constraint; regulators resist shifting costs to homes
reasoning.so_that: A second named frontier lab discloses a gigawatt campus on a multi-decade direct utility deal it funds the grid for
reasoning.landing: by H2 2027; a named lab (Anthropic, xAI, Meta, Google) discloses the deal
reasoning.plain_language: Getting electricity, not chips, now limits AI. So OpenAI signed a 25-year power deal and paid for the grid itself. Other labs will copy it.

summary: OpenAI's Camellia pairs a 3.2-gigawatt Georgia campus with a 25-year utility deal, lab-funded grid infrastructure shielding ratepayers, and demand response. Because grid interconnection now binds frontier compute, a second frontier lab should disclose the same self-financed structure by H2 2027.
